disease_label_per_paper: Complement-mediated thrombotic microangiopathy in a patient with antiphospholipid syndrome and anti-glomerular basement membrane antibodies
presentation_summary: A 30-year-old woman was sent to the ED by nephrology for elevated IgG anti-GBM antibody titer, plasmapheresis initiation, and renal biopsy after creatinine elevation was found during a dry-cough evaluation.

Past history included antiphospholipid antibody syndrome recently treated with apixaban, complex partial epilepsy, migraines with aura, and four pregnancies complicated by preeclampsia or HELLP syndrome.

On arrival, her only symptoms were dry cough and foamy urine. Initial labs showed hemoglobin 11.1 g/dL, creatinine 1.83 mg/dL, platelet count 92000/mm3, LDH 335 U/L, total bilirubin 0.4 mg/dL, and CT chest was unremarkable.

Urinalysis five days before admission showed protein >500 mg/dL without RBCs or RBC casts. She was started on plasmapheresis, IV steroids, heparin bridge, and underwent renal biopsy on hospital day 3.

After biopsy, platelets fell to 40000/mm3, hemoglobin fell to 7.6 g/dL, and ultrasound showed a 5.3 x 2.4 x 6.9 cm hematoma; later evaluation showed low C3/C4, haptoglobin <9 mg/dL, LDH 291 U/L, schistocytes, negative HIT panel, ADAMTS13 61%, and final biopsy with acute and chronic TMA.
Plasmapheresis continued daily; rituximab and eculizumab were started, and she was discharged after 15 days with creatinine trending downward.
